I've confirmed that `intel_display_suspend` doesn't exist in this tree—it's been renamed to `intel_display_driver_suspend`. A broad search across the i915 directory hasn't turned up any references to the old name, so I'll move forward with what I've found.

Looking at the call chain, `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` isn't actually called anywhere; the runtime callback is `intel_runtime_suspend` instead. The data flow I'm tracking is: `i915_drm_suspend(dev)` extracts `dev_priv` via `to_i915(dev)`, then accesses `dev_priv->display` and passes it to `intel_display_driver_suspend(display)`. From my grep results, I can see the function body includes calls to `opregion_target_state`, `intel_display_driver_suspend(display)`, and `i915_gem_suspend(i915)`, which gives me enough to understand the execution order.
## 1. `i915_pm_suspend` — reached from which PCI PM callbacks

`i915_pm_ops` is bound to the PCI driver in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_pci.c`:

```
.driver.pm = &i915_pm_ops,
```

In `drivers/gpu/drm/i915/i915_driver.c` only **two** `dev_pm_ops` slots point at it:

```
.suspend  = i915_pm_suspend,
.poweroff = i915_pm_suspend,
```

Full chains:

```
PCI/PM core
 ├── dev_pm_ops.suspend  ─► i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
 └── dev_pm_ops.poweroff ─► i915_pm_suspend(kdev)
                                 │  i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev)
                                 │  (bails with dev_err "DRM not initialized" if not registered)
                                 └─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
```

Sibling callbacks that reach the same `i915_drm_suspend` *without* going through `i915_pm_suspend` (so they are not part of the chain, but share the leaf):

```
.freeze          ─► i915_pm_freeze        ─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm) + i915_gem_freeze()
i915_driver_shutdown()                    ─► i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm), i915_drm_suspend_late(..., true)
.suspend_late    ─► i915_pm_suspend_late  ─► i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
.suspend_noirq   ─► i915_pm_suspend_noirq ─► i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, false)
.poweroff_late   ─► i915_pm_poweroff_late ─► i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, true)
.poweroff_noirq  ─► i915_pm_poweroff_noirq─► i915_drm_suspend_noirq(&i915->drm, true)
.freeze_late     ─► i915_pm_freeze_late   ─► i915_gem_freeze_late()
```

## 2. Callers that also call `i915_pm_runtime_suspend`

**None.** `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` does not exist in this tree. The runtime-PM hook is named differently:

```
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend,
.runtime_resume  = intel_runtime_resume,
```

`intel_runtime_suspend()` is a peer entry point of `i915_pm_suspend()` in the same `i915_pm_ops`; neither calls the other, and no `i915_pm_*` callback invokes it. They only share state via `dev_priv->runtime_pm` (`intel_runtime_pm_driver_release(rpm)`, wakeref assert enable/disable).

## 3. `dev_priv` data flow: `i915_drm_suspend` → display suspend

Note: `intel_display_suspend()` no longer exists — it was refactored into `intel_display_driver_suspend()` (`display/intel_display_driver.c`), which takes an `struct intel_display *`, not `dev_priv`.

```
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
    struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);        // device -> dev_priv
        │
        └─ i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                        // passes down drm_device
              struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);        // drm_device -> dev_priv
              struct intel_display   *display  = dev_priv->display;    // dev_priv -> display
              │
              ├─ opregion_target_state = suspend_to_idle(dev_priv) ? PCI_D1 : PCI_D3cold;
              ├─ i915_gem_suspend(i915)                        // dev_priv branch
              ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend(display)  ◄── display handle only
              │     state = drm_atomic_helper_suspend(display->drm);   // display -> drm_device
              │     intel_dp_mst_suspend(display);
              ├─ intel_display_driver_suspend_access(display)
              │     intel_dp_mst_suspend(display);
              └─ intel_opregion_suspend(display, opregion_target_state)
```

So `dev_priv` is *not* passed into the display layer: it is dereferenced once in `i915_drm_suspend` (`dev_priv->display`) and only the opaque `struct intel_display *display` crosses the boundary, which internally re-derives the DRM device via `display->drm`.
